title: The AI data center build-out has made the US more reliant than ever on foreign semiconductors
key_facts: New trade figures show the US imported nearly $90.5 billion of chips in the first eight months of 2026, almost twice the $49.2 billion at the same point in 2025.
Semiconductor exports rose by over $10 billion in 2026 but are far outpaced by demand.

In August the US imported semiconductors worth $15.4 (the article omits 'billion') against $7.8 billion of exports, a monthly deficit of $7.6 billion, versus a small surplus of almost $400 million in August 2025.

Grace Zwemmer of Oxford Economics said the trade deficit was boosted by relentless business spending on high-tech goods tied to the AI build-out, and that capital goods imports are up 66% year over year.
She expects capital goods imports to support strong growth in total imports well into 2027.
The 2022 Chips and Science Act put hundreds of billions of government dollars behind US chip manufacturing, and several plants have broken ground.
Yahoo Finance says US factory expansion is not enough to keep up with demand, especially for the most advanced chips needed for frontier AI models.
quote_evidence: New trade deficit figures released this past week show that the US imported nearly $90.5 billion in chips during the first eight months of 2026, almost twice the $49.2 billion brought in at the same point in 2025.
But it's not enough to keep up with the skyrocketing demand for chips, especially the most advanced types of chips needed for frontier AI models.
That is a marked change from a small monthly surplus of almost $400 million in August 2025.
why_it_matters_hint: The AI data-center build-out is pulling in far more imported chips than the US exports, deepening its dependence on foreign chip supply.
event_date: Trade data for August released 6 Oct 2026 (Census release and wire reports of that day); Yahoo Finance analysis 10 Oct 2026.
notes: The article says the data came out 'this past week'; Census, Reuters, CNBC and Yahoo Finance items dated 6 Oct 2026 carry the August trade release, which gives the date. The article prints the August import figure as '$15.4' without 'billion'; $15.4 billion fits the stated $7.8 billion exports and $7.6 billion deficit (15.4 - 7.8 = 7.6). Figures are official government data, the comment is from an Oxford Economics analyst.
